note: Job-seeker version of the 100-point profile rubric from linkedin-agent-skill (MIT). Score honestly: most first-pass profiles land in the 30s and 40s.

items.full_marks: Names the target role and specialty in the words recruiters search for, carries one piece of proof (a result, a domain, a known employer), and uses the 220 characters. Not just a job title, not 'Seeking opportunities', not 'Open to work'.

The first two lines (everything before 'see more') say what I do, for what kind of team, with one concrete proof point. No 'passionate about', no 'results-driven', no third-person bio, does not open with my name.
First person. The problems I solve, one or two real numbers, the tools and skills recruiters filter on, the roles I want next and how to reach me. Under 1,400 characters.
One line of scope, then two or three outcome bullets with numbers. Duties are not outcomes.
The last two roles are detailed with outcomes; anything older than ten years is one line; gaps are explained in a line rather than left blank.
The top three skills are the three I want to be hired for and appear in my target job descriptions; they are endorsed.
Three items: my best post, a portfolio piece (case study, dashboard, GitHub, write-up), and my resume or a way to contact me.
Open to Work is on (recruiters-only if I am employed) with the exact target titles, locations and work types.
A recent photo where my face fills most of the frame and the background is plain.
A banner with one line of positioning, not the default gradient or a stock skyline.
At least three received in the last two years, each naming a specific outcome rather than character.
Posted or commented in the last seven days. An empty activity feed reads as an abandoned profile.
Custom profile URL, location set, and an email in contact info.
